Karaage (からあげ) is a Japanese dish consisting of bite-sized pieces of meat, typically chicken, that are marinated in soy sauce, sake, and spices, then coated in flour or starch and deep-fried. Unlike Western-style fried chicken, which is usually a main course, karaage is often enjoyed as a side dish or appetizer. It’s commonly accompanied by lemon wedges and may also come with condiments such as mayonnaise, soy sauce, vinegar, or spicy mustard.
